note: Decision board, not a work log. Each suggestion states the problem, the candidate paths with their cost and risk, the recommended path and what it depends on. The 'status' field is the control: nothing below is approved until the owner sets it. Silence never approves. Selection controls on the rendered page are stored in the browser only - they change no code and trigger no capture.
review_workflow: Read the problem and the options for a suggestion.
Choose one option, or write your own in the free-text field.
Record the choice locally with the Save button so it survives a reload.
To make it binding, set status for that row in data/lab/suggestions.json to approved and name the approver. Only that edit changes what the project will do.
rows: SG-01
Decide the price source first, and let everything else queue behind it

Eleven of the requirements on the readiness table are blocked by the absence of a market price. Building more strategy scaffolding before that is decided produces more empty columns, not more capability.
A) License a vendor feed - cost: money and a contract; risk: redistribution terms may forbid what we want to publish
B) Exchange or broker API - cost: integration; risk: liquidity and timing differ from the sportsbook market we would actually bet
C) Self-capture one operator with written permission - cost: engineering and a fragile parser; risk: terms, and a single-book view is not a market
D) Research-only: never take a price - cost: no backtest, no ROI, no CLV ever; risk: none of the performance requirements can be met
D until the owner chooses otherwise, then re-cost A and C in that order. Publishing no number is cheaper than publishing a wrong one.

1 decision
none if D; contractual if A
proposed
Whether the project is a research layer or a trading operation - which decides the next six months

Stand up the scheduled availability snapshot runner before adding a single depth feature
One capture exists. Every requirement that needs a change over time - injury as surprise, the timestamped series, the weekly diff, the point-in-time ledger - is undefined with a single observation.
A) Scheduled runner, Wed/Thu/Fri plus game day, append-only with content hashes - cost: a runner and a store; risk: terms of capture
B) Daily capture - cost: more storage; risk: same terms question, more rows to reconcile
C) Weekly only - cost: nothing new; risk: deltas stay impossible and the surprise signal never exists
A, but only after Q-PRICE-02 and Q-STORE-01 are answered, because the runner writes the data whose storage policy is undecided.

The brief asks for 2nd/3rd/4th-string replacements on both sides of the ball. No official source read this session publishes a replacement. Building the feature anyway means inventing a starter.
A) Per-club official depth pages, verified 32/32 before use - cost: slow, and at least one club publishes depth as an image; risk: coverage gaps block the feature
B) Snap counts from official Game Books as the starter proxy - cost: PDF parsing at scale; risk: a proxy is not a club's stated depth
C) Publish absences only and refuse to name replacements - cost: the deficiency matrix stays empty; risk: none

B) Parse and retain the PDFs as well - cost: storage; risk: redistribution terms
C) Do not parse - cost: R-25, R-31, R-44 and R-53 stay blocked; risk: none

Both captures this session were transcribed from live pages that will change layout without notice. A silent parse failure looks exactly like a quiet week.

SG-11
Type every absence: listed, reserve, or unknown
A player on injured reserve produces no row on the weekly report. Treating 'no row' as 'available' is a silent, systematic error in exactly the direction that inflates a team's health.
A) Join a reserve list so absence is typed - cost: another capture; risk: terms
B) Type every report absence as 'unknown' rather than 'available' - cost: a less useful table; risk: none
C) Do nothing and keep reading absence as availability - cost: none; risk: systematic bias in every availability feature
B immediately, A as soon as the reserve source is confirmed. Option C is the error this suggestion exists to remove.

The train/validation/holdout split is inside a single 2026 season. Roster context and the new kickoff regime leak across folds.

B) Keep the within-season split and publish the limitation - cost: nothing; risk: optimistic validation
C) Do not use the holdout until a season-level split exists - cost: nothing is validated; risk: none
A is the goal; B is what is published now with the limitation stated on the results page; C is the safe default if A never happens.

SG-14
Add the stadium roof/surface and NWS weather overlay only after the roof source is found
Two Week 10 fixtures were played in Munich and one in Madrid this season alone, so venue context is not a rounding error. But half a weather feature is worse than none.
A) Find the official roof designation source, then wire NWS hourly per venue - cost: one lookup plus a forecast job; risk: none if the source is official
B) Use NWS only and treat roof as unknown - cost: less work; risk: a closed roof makes wind irrelevant and an assumed-outdoor model wrong
C) No weather features - cost: totals and passing props may misprice in wind; risk: none of fabrication
C until the roof source is confirmed, then A. Option B should be avoided: it looks rigorous while assuming the one thing that matters.

SG-18
Name the approver before the board has anything to approve

The suggestions board currently has no named approver, so a decision and a comment look identical in the file. Adding one while there are 18 rows to decide is cheaper than adding one after the first dispute.
A) Name a single approver in the governance block - cost: one line; risk: a bottleneck if that person is unavailable
B) Two-person rule for anything touching data capture or publication - cost: one more name; risk: slower decisions
C) Leave it unnamed and decide ad hoc - cost: nothing; risk: the last editor of a file becomes the decision maker
A now, with B as the escalation for anything touching capture or the publication boundary. It belongs in the readiness table so it is visible rather than implied.
